(j) "extant variety" means a variety available in India which is—

1. not derived from an unpatented plant variety, and
2. either identical with or sufficiently similar to any other registered variety so as to be indistinguishable therefrom by ordinary observation or by simple technical means; provided that the differences between such varieties are due solely to the act of derivation and do not affect the essential characteristics resulting from the genotype or combination of genotypes of such initial variety.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, the Central Government may make rules to provide for all or any of the following matters: (a) the procedure for registration of copyright; (b) the form of applications for copyright registration and other documents required therefor; (c) the fees payable in respect of such registrations and applications; (d) the conditions under which a person may be granted an extension of time to file necessary documents or pay prescribed fees; (e) the manner of publication of notices relating to copyright matters; (f) the format, content, and maintenance of registers of copyrights.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, the Central Government may make rules to provide for all or any of the following matters: (a) the procedure for registration of copyright; (b) the form of complaints and applications to be made, and the licences to be granted under this Act; (c) the fees payable in respect of such registrations, complaints, and applications; (d) the conditions subject to which a licence may be issued or refused; (e) the manner in which any dispute arising out of the interpretation or application of this Act shall be resolved.

Whereas it is necessary to provide for the payment of certain fees under this Act, hereinafter referred to as "fees", there shall be levied and collected by the Authority such fees in respect of applications made under this Act. The fees so payable may vary from time to time as notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette. Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, any person making an application for registration or seeking any other relief under this Act shall pay the prescribed fee along with the application. Provided that where a fee is not paid within the stipulated period, the Authority may reject the application without prejudice to its validity and effect.

Whereas it is necessary to provide for the payment of certain fees under this Act, hereinafter referred to as "fees", there shall be a fee payable by any person seeking registration or certification in respect of a plant variety. Such fees shall be prescribed and collected by the Authority. The Authority may also impose additional fees for specific services such as re-examination, rectification, or extension of protection. Any person aggrieved by an order regarding the imposition or collection of fees may appeal to the Appellate Board within thirty days from the date of receipt of notice of such order.

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, "broadcast reproduction right" means the exclusive right to communicate by wireless signs, signals, sounds, or device any broadcast signal containing an adaptation, translation, or other form of the work to the public. Subject to the provisions contained in this Act, the owner of copyright in a work shall have the sole authority to authorize or prohibit the exercise of such broadcast reproduction right. Any person who without authorization exercises the said right shall be liable for infringement and may be ordered by any court to desist from further infringement and to pay damages as may be determined by the court.

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,—(a) "benefit sharing" means the distribution and utilization by the farmer community of any financial benefits arising out of the use of plant varieties for which registration has been granted under this Act; (b) "farmer community" includes traditional farmers who have contributed to the development or improvement of such plant variety through their knowledge, skills, and practices. Subject to the provisions of this Act, a breeder shall ensure that any financial benefits accruing from the use of a registered variety are shared with the farmer community in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority.

Where any offence under this Act has been committed by a director of a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed was responsible for the conduct of business or affairs of the said company as well as such director shall be deemed to be guilty of such offence and may be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this subsection shall affect the liability of any other person under this Act. Where a licence is granted by the Controller, it shall not be valid unless executed on behalf of the company by its duly authorised officer or director as specified in the licence. Any such execution without authority from the said officer or director shall render both the executing party and the director liable to penalties provided for in this Act.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any international agreement including the Patent Cooperation Treaty to which India is a party, where an applicant desires to obtain patent protection in more than one country, he shall file with the Controller a single international application under such treaty or agreement. The international application shall be made in accordance with the rules and procedures prescribed by the Controller for this purpose. Provided that the Controller may accept an international application filed within twelve months from the filing date of the first national patent application, provided such application is filed in India.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any international agreement including the Patent Cooperation Treaty, every applicant for a patent shall make his application in such form and manner as may be prescribed. The Controller may, at any time before grant of a patent, require the applicant to furnish such further particulars or information as may be necessary for the purpose of examining the application under this Act. If the Controller is satisfied that an international application has been made by an Indian resident or a company incorporated in India and complies with the requirements of the Patent Cooperation Treaty, he shall treat it as a national application filed in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
